summary.text: April Worsley is second on the Victorian Socialists' Southern Metropolitan Region ticket for the Legislative Council at the 2026 election. Her party page says she is a former school teacher who has been active in Palestine solidarity and anti-racism campaigns and has joined workers' picket lines. She calls for a rent freeze, full funding of public services and a move away from fossil fuels.

priorities.text: A freeze on rents
Proper funding for public schools, hospitals and childcare
Closing fossil fuel companies and moving fully to renewable energy

summary.text: David Davis is a Liberal member of the Legislative Council, elected for East Yarra Province in 1996 and representing Southern Metropolitan Region since that province was abolished in 2006. He was Minister for Health and Ageing and Leader of the Government in the Council from 2010 to 2014, and has led the Liberals in the upper house in three separate spells, most recently from December 2024 to November 2025. He now holds the shadow energy, resources and arts portfolios, and is recontesting Southern Metropolitan in 2026.

summary.text: Melissa Lowe is running as a community independent for Southern Metropolitan Region in the Legislative Council at the 2026 election; her campaign site says Voices groups in Ashwood and Malvern asked her to stand. She contested Hawthorn as a teal independent in 2022 and lost to the Liberals' John Pesutto. With Paul Hopper she was a plaintiff in Hopper v Victoria, in which the High Court in April 2026 struck down Part 12 of Victoria's Electoral Act, the political donations scheme. Her background is in education equity work, including diversity and inclusion at Holmesglen TAFE and programs at Swinburne University.

summary.text: Xavier Boffa is third on the Liberal ticket for Southern Metropolitan Region in the Legislative Council at the 2026 Victorian election, after David Davis and Georgie Crozier. He describes himself as a lawyer and public policy professional, and he studied arts, public policy and law at the University of Melbourne. In June 2020 he became the Samuel Griffith Society's first full-time executive director; before that he advised John Pesutto when Pesutto was shadow attorney-general, and he has also worked for a US congressman in Washington.

prior_roles.role: Principal parliamentary and portfolio adviser to the Shadow Attorney-General, John Pesutto
Staff member in the Washington, D.C. office of US Congressman Ted Yoho

legal_and_integrity.text: Charged with assaulting a fellow Liberal student member at an Adelaide bar during the Australian Liberal Students' Federation's annual meeting in July 2019
legal_and_integrity.outcome: Acquitted in the Adelaide Magistrates' Court; the party took no action while the case was pending
legal_and_integrity.note: Matched by name: Wikipedia identifies the Xavier Boffa in this case as a former president of the Australian Liberal Students' Federation and of the Melbourne University Liberal Club, and the candidate studied at the University of Melbourne; his own site doesn't mention it.

priorities.text: Easing cost-of-living pressure, which he links to his own experience of running a business and starting a family
Making housing more affordable
Improving Victoria's economic outlook
